review_notes: Mined verifier: 13 checks, 6 tagged incidental (note_exists, note_prose_floor, note_reducer, note_reducer_exactly_one, note_coupler, note_coupler_exactly_one), 2 existence-only, C-03 graded in a separate check, note checks were long brittle regexes. Forward map now: header (register_header), every row's fitting_id and kind plus population and order (register_table), counts and total (results_figures), note counts (note_reducer_count, note_coupler_count), each unresolved connection named (note_unresolved_C-10, note_unresolved_C-24). Backward: no check grades an unasked thing. Delivery Gate (layer5 coverage_depth, surface_form_brittleness) then showed the note checks were co-occurrence only: 'We need 11 couplers and 3 reducers' passed both count checks, 'C-10 is resolved, C-24 unresolved' passed note_unresolved_C-10, and register_table casefolded fitting_id/fitting_kind so a lower-case register passed despite the capitals rule. Gate round 2 (requirement_traceability, surface_form_brittleness) then found the round-1 fix too strict: banning the word 'resolved' and fitting words near a count were rules submission_format.md never states ('C-10 is unresolved (not resolved yet)' and 'C-10 and C-24 cannot be resolved yet; both are unresolved' failed). Gate round 3 (representation_contract, surface_form_brittleness) found two more over-strict forms: 'no other number between a count and its word' ('11 of the 24 runs take reducers' failed) and a list joiner without line breaks ('C-10\nC-24 are unresolved' failed). Gate round 4 (surface_form_brittleness, brittle_prose_matcher): the unresolved list joiner was a closed set of punctuation, 'and' and line breaks, so 'C-10 with C-24 are unresolved' failed note_unresolved_C-10 although submission_format.md does not restrict how the unresolved connections are listed together.
change_made: tests/verifier.json rebuilt as 7 core checks generated from the gold; note checks accept either order, digits or number words, any case, and grouped unresolved IDs; every why_justification quotes the sentence it enforces; incidental and existence-only checks removed. Round 2 (checks only; instruction, inputs and gold byte-identical): register_header case-sensitive; register_table grades fitting_id and fitting_kind with cell type id (case preserved); each note count must be the number stated for its word (no other number or fitting word between, no hedge, not bound to another fitting word); an unresolved id must not be called 'resolved'. Regenerated by tests/generate_fixture.py; tests/manifest.json still byte-identical. Round 3 (checks only; inputs and gold byte-identical): the 'resolved' ban and the fitting-word ban removed. Unresolved checks now enforce the stated rule exactly: only unresolved connections listed together with the id (commas, 'and', '&', '/') may stand between it and 'unresolved'. Count checks: no other number between the count and its word; a number directly bound to another fitting word or given as a hedge is not the count. Round 4 (checks only; inputs and gold byte-identical): count checks ban only a competing count (a number attached to another fitting word) between a count and its word, plus the count being attached to another fitting word or hedged; the unresolved joiner accepts line breaks, bullets, semicolons and a parenthetical after an id. Round 5 (checks only; inputs and gold byte-identical): the unresolved list joiner also accepts English list words ('with', 'plus', 'or', 'along with', 'together with', 'as well as', 'including', 'connection C-24', up to four in a row) and en/em dashes.
